newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares mixed to weak in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares mixed to weak in quiet trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares were mixed to weak in a generally inactive market as most players sat on the sidelines ahead of the expected release next week of annual inflation figures for September.
"I think people are just sitting waiting for the inflation figures for September to show which way inflation is going following the surprise fall in August's figure," one broker said.

Zimbabwe's annual inflation fell to a three-year low of 17.7 percent in August, taking many local economists by surprise. Most of them had expected it to track upwards due to a spate of price hikes in July.
The surprise fall boosted hopes of cuts in interest rates and this fuelled a bull-run on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange.

The bulls ran out of steam three weeks ago, hit by a wave of profit-taking and also doubts that the southern African country would sustain lower annual inflation after the government last week raised fuel prices for the third time this year.

On the market on Monday, the key industrial index edged 2.63 points lower to close at 6,783.38, depressed mainly by clothing retailer Truworths' 50-cent drop to 600 and cable manufacturer BICAF's 30-cent loss to 350.
Also among the losers, food and wine producer Cairns shed 25 cents to 805, sugar refinery ZSR lost 20 cents to 1,250 and tea producer Tanganda traded 10 cents down at 150.

Against the trend, tyre producer Dunlop rose 20 cents to 190 while finance house UDC at 225, local conglomerate TA Holdings at 135, brickmaker and engineering firm Mash at 145 and pork processor Colcom at 300 all added five cents.
Minings were largely unchanged except for weakened bids in gold producer Ashanti and Wankie Colliery. The mining index was unmoved at 1,368.98.
